nodes.question: How much performance improvement, measured in mIoU, is achieved by merging different-architecture models with a shared backbone?
nodes.answer: Merging different-architecture models with a shared backbone achieves a performance improvement of 6.8% in mIoU.
nodes.paragraph: Experimental results demonstrate substantial UDA improvements without additional costs for merging same-architecture models from distinct datasets ( 2.6% mloU) and different-architecture models with a shared backbone ( 6.8% mloU). Furthermore, merging semantic and panoptic segmen-t tation models increases mPQ by 7%. These ndings are validated across a wide variety of UDA strategies, architectures and datasets. The code will be publicly available upon acceptance in the LWMM repository: http://www-vpu.eps.uam.es/LWMM/ . Keywords Model merging Unsupervised domain adaptation Semantic segmentation Panoptic segmentation Synthetic data 1 Introduction Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to train models from a source labeled domain that can generalize to an unla- beled target domain, key for tasks with limited annotated data due to the capture dif culty or the high annotation costs (e.g.,semantic or panoptic segmentation [ 1]). Thus, automatically annotated synthetic datasets emerge as attractive alternative for the source domain for segmentation tasks [ 2 6]. While Roberto Alcover-Couso work done prior to joining Amazon. nodes.question: What performance improvements were observed in the research when merging models from different architectures with shared parameters?
